# Harness Relay

> Harness Relay is a local task assistant: the coding agents you already have work with you and with each other in one chat. It runs the real agent CLIs with your own sign-ins: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI and Muse Code, and five open-source coding agents (OpenCode, Goose, Cline, OpenHands and Pi) on the model backends you choose. One kind of agent is enough for a team.

- For each question, a lead agent picks a team from your templates, adapts one or designs a new one (roles, models, reasoning effort and turn order). You confirm it before the team starts (unless you let the lead agent's team start without asking); once the team has answered, the lead agent can review the replies and mark what needs your attention.
- Team checks: one set of rules for the whole team in Edit and Full access chats. Harness Relay checks protected paths, commit format and commands such as npm test. In parallel mode, it runs the commands on a copy of the working directory before applying a member's result. Most agents also refuse writes to protected paths. On macOS and Linux, hooks run around supported tool calls for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Muse Code and Pi. A before hook that fails refuses the call. An after hook's failure goes back to the agent.
- Three ways to take turns: Roundtable (agents speak in order, in rounds, each seeing what the earlier ones said), Parallel (all at once, independently; in edit mode each agent works in its own git worktree) and Relay (one agent at a time, handing off by @mentioning a teammate).
- Each chat has a permission: Read-only, Edit or Full access. Anything beyond it waits in the chat for your approval, and agents can ask you a question and wait for the answer. In edit mode each working directory becomes a git repository, and every reply shows the files it changed with a diff.
- The agent CLIs send prompts to the models (only Labs' reading in parts, when you turn it on, has Harness Relay ask a model of your Model connections itself). The proprietary CLIs run with their own sign-ins (Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Copilot can also run on your own endpoint), and the open-source agents use your API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI) or your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint. In Settings → Model connections, expand Custom endpoints, enter the base URL and optional key, click Load models, select model IDs and save. Saving checks selected and manually entered IDs against the catalog or per-model metadata. If neither is available for any ID, the user can confirm saving unverified IDs. The server listens on 127.0.0.1 and keeps its data on your computer: conversations and settings in one SQLite database, attachments as files, and API keys, MCP server tokens, mail and calendar passwords and the tokens of the MCP servers and calendars you sign in to in the OS credential store (or encrypted in the database where there is none).
- Automations send the team a message when you run one, at set times, when something happens (a new mail in one of your accounts, an event about to begin, a pull request or a failed CI run on GitHub, a file in the working directory; Harness Relay checks it itself), or when a program on your computer (a git hook, a CI runner) calls its webhook, with what it posted; in the same chat or a new one each time. One can track a goal across runs: each run is told the goal and what earlier runs reported, says where it stands, and the automation switches off once it is reached; a run that fails is tried again.
- New chat and New automation have a Common apps picker in the composer. It offers the apps available to the selected assistants and permission level, including Slack, Teams, Google Drive, Notion, Heptabase, Obsidian and GitHub. A proposed Google Docs or Obsidian write goes to the outbox for preview and confirmation before it changes the document or note.
- A tool library of MCP servers, skills and memory, set up once, reaches every agent, and its hooks are what new chats start with; an MCP server that signs in with OAuth (Linear, Notion, Atlassian and others) signs in from it, and at each turn its members get a short-lived access token. Through one MCP server of its own, Harness Relay also gives every agent (Grok, Muse Code, and the open-source agents but OpenCode, in full access only) its own tools: a headless browser of its own for each chat (each new site asked about below full access), and your mail and calendar. Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive use the Google desktop OAuth client saved in Common apps. Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com mail and calendars use Microsoft OAuth. Relay keeps tokens in the OS credential store. iCloud uses an app-specific password. Microsoft Teams uses a work or school account with Microsoft Graph PowerShell. Its Common apps row can install PowerShell 7, and each proposed Teams message waits in the outbox for approval. A mail or an invitation never goes out in the turn: it waits in the outbox, a card in the chat, until you click Send.
- Settings & sign-in → Labs holds experimental ways for agents to use Harness Relay's own tools, off by default and one at a time: letting agents script the tools (CodeAct: a short JavaScript program whose every tool call is decided as the agent's own, run in Harness Relay's own sandbox with no network), or reading long texts in parts (RLM: the same, with a text kept for the turn and questions to a model you choose, billed on its key, up to 100 a turn). Neither works on Windows.
- Below full access, the open-source agents run in Harness Relay's own OS sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux); on native Windows they run only with full access, and so does OpenCode on Linux.
- It comes as a desktop app for macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows (x64 and Arm64) and Linux (x64 and Arm64), or runs from source on Node.js 22.13 or later. From Settings & sign-in you can install and connect one assistant, then open New chat and ask a first question. It can also be tried in a GitHub codespace of your own, with nothing to install. The interface is in English and Traditional Chinese (繁體中文).
- License: the Sustainable Use License 1.0, a source-available license, not an OSI-approved open-source one. It allows use and changes for your own internal business purposes or for non-commercial or personal use, free of charge.

## Website

- [Harness Relay](https://agentic-system-lab.github.io/harness-relay/): the landing page in English, with use cases and downloads
- [Harness Relay（繁體中文）](https://agentic-system-lab.github.io/harness-relay/zh-TW/): the same page in Traditional Chinese
- [Use cases](https://agentic-system-lab.github.io/harness-relay/use-cases/): twelve real recorded examples to use as a starting point for your own tasks, including a bug fixed three ways in parallel worktrees, a one-page product spec (PRD) from five customer interviews, launch copy from competitors’ pricing pages, a month-end bank reconciliation, overdue invoices chased by an automation with a goal, a brief written before each customer call by an automation that waits for the calendar, a literature review with sources, a quiz tried on a student, a contract redlined on Qwen3.8 served by your own vLLM, an alert triaged from a webhook, a design review of screenshots, and an app’s strings translated by Antigravity, back-translated by Copilot and checked by Claude Code each time the English file changes
- [使用情境（繁體中文）](https://agentic-system-lab.github.io/harness-relay/zh-TW/use-cases/): the same twelve examples in Traditional Chinese
- [Docs](https://agentic-system-lab.github.io/harness-relay/docs/): how to use the app, a page per task, for people who use it rather than work on it: installing it, connecting the agents, the first chat (with a link to the full demo), teams and modes, permissions and approvals, conversations, automations, tools, using it from a phone and troubleshooting
- [文件（繁體中文）](https://agentic-system-lab.github.io/harness-relay/zh-TW/docs/): the same docs in Traditional Chinese

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay/main/README.md): overview, features, requirements, the desktop app and running from source
- [User guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay/main/docs/user-guide.md): every feature step by step, and installing and signing in to each agent CLI
- [Open-source agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay/main/docs/open-agents.md): OpenCode, Goose, Cline, OpenHands and Pi, their model backends and Harness Relay's own sandbox
- [Sandboxing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay/main/docs/sandboxing.md): every OS sandbox the agents run in, by platform
- [Try it in GitHub Codespaces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay/main/docs/codespaces.md): what a codespace runs, what it costs and how to start one
- [Remote access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay/main/docs/remote-access.md): using Harness Relay from your phone through Tailscale
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay/main/docs/architecture.md): components, turn scheduling, the CLI adapters, approvals, security and known limitations
